the optimal duration of CPR guided by AMSA is associated with improved outcome of CPR.
the optimal duration of CPR guided by AMSA before defibrillation can improve the outcome of CPR, even in a model of prolonged VF.

the development of a novel method for the detection of cardiac arrest and the determination of the optimal time to defibrillate in the setting of cardiac arrest.
a novel method of determining optimal duration of CPR based on the AMSA algorithm.
the development of a novel method to guide the duration of CPR before defibrillation in prolonged cardiac arrest.

the optimal duration of CPR guided by AMSA before defibrillation improves outcome of CPR in the setting of a prolonged cardiac arrest in a rat model.
AMSA guided CPR is superior to guidelines based CPR in the setting of a prolonged cardiac arrest in a rat model.
the optimal duration of CPR guided by AMSA is superior to the current guidelines based algorithms in a model of prolonged cardiac arrests.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the duration of CPR should be guided by AMSA to improve the outcome of CPR after prolonged cardiac arrest.

AMSA guided CPR duration prior to defibrillations improves ROSC and post resuscitation outcomes in the setting of a prolonged cardiac arrest.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the duration of CPR before defibrillation should be guided by AMSA and not by guidelines based with immediate defibrillation.
